title: HashMark receipt
description: A pointer to a HashMark record on the Radiant blockchain. A receipt is NEVER evidence on its own: a verifier must fetch the referenced transaction and output, decode it per HASHMARK_PROTOCOL.md, and report the on-chain values rather than the receipt's. Schema validity means only that the document is well-formed enough to be worth looking up.

format.description: Fixed discriminator identifying this document type.

version.description: Receipt schema version. A higher value is not corruption: it means the receipt is newer than the verifier, which should say so rather than reporting the file as broken.

network.description: The chain the transaction lives on. Authoritative identity comes from genesisHash when present; this field is the human-readable name.

algorithm.description: Hash algorithm named by the on-chain record. Determines the required digest length.

digest.description: The file digest as lowercase hexadecimal. Uppercase is invalid rather than normalized, so a digest has exactly one accepted spelling. Length must match the algorithm: 64 characters for sha256.

transactionId.description: Radiant transaction id, 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

outputIndex.description: Index of the output carrying the HashMark record. Conventionally 0, but never assume it.

label.description: The optional public label as recorded on-chain. Note the on-chain limit is 128 UTF-8 BYTES; maxLength here counts characters, so it is a loose upper bound only — the byte-length check happens against the decoded record. Must be escaped before display.

genesisHash.description: Block 0 hash of the chain, lowercase hex. Optional but strongly recommended: it binds the receipt to a chain by identity rather than by name, so a testnet receipt cannot be read as a mainnet proof. When present it must agree with 'network'.

expectedSigner.description: The signer the reader should EXPECT for a v2 mark, as a base58check address. Not a claim about who signed: the record commits to a signer of its own, and the chain wins. A mismatch is a disagreement to report, never grounds to reject the record, and a match is not evidence in itself because anyone can write a receipt. Absent for v1 marks, which carry no signer. Compare by decoded (version byte, hash160), never as base58 strings. This pattern checks shape only; the checksum is verified when the address is decoded.
